'''Rata''' was the [[second officer]] of the [[Ferengi]] {{Class|D'Kora}} [[Bok's Marauder|marauder]] commanded by [[DaiMon]] [[Bok]] in [[2364]]. 

That year, he was involved in the plan to return the {{USS|Stargazer|NCC-2893}} to [[Starfleet]] and helped Bok in the plot to avenge the death of Bok's son who was killed in a battle with the ''Stargazer'' in [[2355]], commanded by [[Jean-Luc Picard]]. He helped alter the ''Stargazer''{{'}}s logs to make it appear that Picard had attacked an unarmed ship. Unknown to Rata, Bok also employed a [[thought maker|mind-altering device]] to make Picard [[beam]] to his old ship and relive the [[Battle of Maxia|battle]], only this time he was attacking the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-D|-D}}, his new command. After the plot was foiled, Rata and [[First Officer]] [[Kazago]] arrested Bok because there was no profit in revenge. ({{TNG|The Battle}})

{{bginfo|Rata was played by actor [[Robert Towers]].}}

{{sidebar individual |image = Talak'talan.jpg |caption = Talak'talan (2370) |species = [[Jem'Hadar]] |affiliation = [[Dominion]] |rank = {{dis|Third|rank}} |occupation = [[Soldier]] |status = Active |datestatus = 2370 |actor = [[Cress Williams]] }} '''Talak'talan''' was a [[Jem'Hadar]] in service of the [[Dominion]] during the late-[[24th century]]. ==History== In [[2370]], Talak'talan held the rank of {{dis|Third|rank}} when he and his unit took [[Commander]] [[Benjamin Sisko]] and [[Quark]] prisoner on a [[planet]] in the [[Gamma Quadrant]]. Representing the Dominion, he boarded [[Deep Space 9]] to personally inform [[Starfleet]] of the fact and to give them a list of [[Alpha Quadrant]] ships and colonies the Jem'Hadar had destroyed, stating that the Dominion would no longer tolerate ships crossing to "their" side of the [[Bajoran wormhole|wormhole]]. ({{DS9|The Jem'Hadar}}) ==Memorable quotes== "''We don't know who you're talking about. We are not your enemies.''"
"''Then you'd better run.''"
"''It's too late. You're done running.''"
'''Benjamin Sisko''', '''Eris''' and '''Talak'talan''' "''A Ferengi and a Human. I was hoping the first race I'd meet from the other side of the anomaly would be the Klingons.''"
"''I'm sorry to disappoint you.''"
:- '''Talak'talan''' and '''Benjamin Sisko''' "''I'm Third Talak'Talan of the Jem'Hadar. I'm here to inform you that your commander has been detained for questioning by the Dominion.''"
"''Detained? For how long?''"
"''Indefinitely. Commander Sisko will serve as an example of what happens to anyone who interferes with the Dominion.''"
:- '''Talak'talan''' and '''Kira Nerys''' "''You should be proud. I hear they fought well for a spiritual people. I hope we won't have to repeat this lesson.''" :- '''Talak'talan''', on the destruction of [[New Bajor]] ==Appendices== ===Background information=== Talak'talan was played by actor [[Cress Williams]] and was the first Jem'Hadar seen in ''[[Star Trek]]''. The final script for {{e|The Jem'Hadar}} gives the pronunciation of Talak'talan's name as "tuh-LOCK tuh-LON". He is described thusly: "''Talak'talan, like all Jem'Hadar, carries himself with a certain relaxed confidence. He's not the kind of stiff-backed spit-and-polish Cardassian soldier we're used to. Nor does he swagger like a Klingon. He knows he's the best, and has nothing to prove. Among Talak'talan's military gear and paraphernalia, there's a tube running up from his uniform into his neck. This tube is common to all the Jem'Hadar''". {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/446.txt}} Talak'talan's ability to walk through a raised force field was never seen again in ''Deep Space Nine''. In his review of the episode, ''Star Trek'' author [[Keith R.A. DeCandido]] described Williams' performance as "great work" and "especially scary". {{el|http://www.tor.com/2013/10/08/star-trek-deep-space-nine-rewatch-the-jemhadar/}} ===Apocrypha=== In the non-canon {{video game}} ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine - Dominion Wars|Dominion Wars]]'', Talak'talan is among the many thousands of Jem'Hadar who travel through the wormhole to Cardassia prior to the start of the [[Dominion War|the war itself]]. He is promoted to [[Jem'Hadar ranks#First|First]] with [[Jem'Hadar ranks#Second|Second]] [[Goran'Agar]] in his unit, and aids in the capture of Deep Space 9 during the war. The ''[[Echoes and Refractions]]'' short story "A Gutted World" tells the story of Talak'talan in an alternate timeline. Talak'talan is also featured in the ''[[Star Trek Customizable Card Game]]''. ===External links=== * {{mbeta}} [[cs:Talak'talan]] [[de:Talak'talan]] [[es:Talak'talan]] [[nl:Talak'talan]] [[Category:Jem'Hadar]] [[Category:Dominion personnel]]

{{sidebar individual |image = Ometiklan.jpg |caption = Omet'iklan (2372) |species = [[Jem'Hadar]] |affiliation = [[Dominion]] |rank = {{dis|First|rank}} |occupation = First in command of an unit under [[Vorta]] [[Weyoun 4|Weyoun]] |status = Active |datestatus = 2372 |actor = [[Clarence Williams III]] }} {{aquote|I am First Omet'iklan, and I am dead. As of this moment, we are all dead. We go into battle to reclaim our lives. This we do gladly, for we are Jem'Hadar. Remember, victory is life.|Omet'iklan|2372|To the Death}} '''Omet'iklan''' was a [[Jem'Hadar]] in service of the [[Dominion]] during the late [[24th century]]. ==History== In [[2372]], Omet'iklan was {{dis|First|rank}} of a unit under the [[Vorta]] [[Weyoun 4|Weyoun]], whose [[Jem'Hadar attack ship|attack ship]] was set upon by a group of rogue Jem'Hadar who had seized an [[Iconian gateway]] on [[Vandros IV]]. Omet'iklan and five of his surviving men were [[transporter|transported]] aboard the {{USS|Defiant|2370}} before their ship exploded. Under Weyoun's orders, Omet'iklan reluctantly agreed to a joint mission with the ''Defiant'' officers to destroy the gateway on Vandros IV. Omet'iklan regarded the Vorta with contempt for their belief that the Jem'Hadar's loyalty can only be kept by deception and [[ketracel-white]]. Omet'iklan was a vicious disciplinarian who killed his {{dis|Second|rank}}, [[Toman'torax]], for attacking [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Worf]]. When Sisko refused to do the same to Worf, Omet'iklan promised to kill Sisko when the mission was over. As the mission progressed, Worf expressed his concerns over the threat the captain had received. Worf even suggested that Sisko stay on the ship during the away mission, which he refused to do. Consequently, Worf warned the captain not to turn his back on his enemy. Worf went on to "reassure" Sisko that if Omet'iklan should kill him that Worf would make certain that Omet'iklan would not live long enough to boast about it to anyone. Captain Sisko, for his part, smiled slightly, saying that he was "very comforted" at the idea. During the attack against the rebel Jem'Hadar, Sisko saved Omet'iklan's life, which surprised him. After they successfully accomplished their mission, Omet'iklan killed Weyoun for questioning his loyalty earlier by attempting to withhold the information about the gateway. Omet'iklan did not carry out his threat to kill Sisko, but he did tell him that the next time they met it would be as enemies. He and his unit elected to remain on Vandros IV to hunt down the remaining rogue Jem'Hadar. ({{DS9|To the Death}}) [[2374|Two years later]], following the outbreak of [[Dominion War|full-scale war]], Sisko recalled Omet'iklan's actions to [[Remata'Klan]], whose unit had [[crash]]ed on the same deserted planet, hoping to turn him against his treacherous Vorta, [[Keevan]] (who hoped to see the Jem'Hadar die before they ran out of white and killed everything in their path, including him) - he was unsuccessful, and Remata'klan was killed in a suicidal attack. ({{DS9|Rocks and Shoals}}) ==Memorable quotes== "''If you're looking for your weapons, they were removed in transport.''"
"''Even without weapons, we're more than a match for you.''"
:- '''Benjamin Sisko''' and '''Omet'iklan''' "''...the only thing I despise more than the Federation is a Jem'Hadar soldier who breaks his vow of allegiance.''"
:- '''Omet'iklan''' to Benjamin Sisko "''Are you accusing me of something?''"
"''It is not for us to accuse a god of betraying heaven. The gods themselves will sit in judgement over you.''"
"''I'm no god, and neither are the Founders. The sooner you realize that, the better off you'll be.''"
:- '''Odo''' and '''Omet'klan''', of Odo's opposition to the Dominion "''In battle, nothing is certain.''"
:- '''Omet'iklan''' "''You think you have to lie to us and use the white to ensure our loyalty. But the fact is, we are more loyal to the Founders than the Vorta ever will. It is the reason for our existence. It is the core of our being.''"
"''There's an entire company of Jem'Hadar down on Vandros Four who would disagree with you.''"
"''And for that, they will die.''"
:- '''Omet'iklan''' and '''Weyoun''' "''I threatened to kill you, but you were still willing to sacrifice yourself to save my life.''"
"''Looks that way.''"
"''Why?''"
"''If you have to ask, you'll never understand.''"
:- '''Omet'klan''' and '''Benjamin Sisko''' ==Appendices== ===Background information=== Omet'iklan was played by actor [[Clarence Williams III]]. The script for {{e|To the Death}} gives the pronunciation of Omet'klan's name as "oh-MET-i-klon". Of his first on-screen appearance, it goes on to describe him as, "''...unimpressed, he is a consummate professional soldier who's been in combat his entire life. He's been in far worse situations than this one.''" {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/496.txt}} Director [[LeVar Burton]] had Williams in mind to play the character from the start. "''He's an old friend of mine, but we'd never worked together before.''" he explained. "''This was just an opportunity to say, 'Hey CW, you want to come and do this thing?{{'}}''" ({{ds9c|347}}) Producer [[Ronald D. Moore]] really enjoyed Williams' take on the character; "''I liked Clarence Williams III, I always have, and I thought he really personified the Jem'Hadar for the first time in a way that the audience could grab onto. The Jem'Hadar in a lot of the episodes tend to kind of bland out. Sometimes it's hard to differentiate between them, and'' [Williams] ''brought something to that performance that made him at least stand alone among that race.''" (''[[Captains' Logs Supplemental - The Unauthorized Guide to the New Trek Voyages]]'', p.120) Similarly, ''[[Star Trek]]'' author [[Keith R.A. DeCandido]] wrote that Williams "''knocks it out of the park as Omet'iklan.''" Of the character itself he opined, "''Omet’iklan is the wise, ruthless leader, the brutal strategist, the loyal soldier—but his loyalty is to the Founders, not the Vorta, whom he holds in obvious contempt.''" {{el|http://www.tor.com/blogs/2014/04/star-trek-deep-space-nine-rewatch-to-the-death}} ===Apocrypha=== [[File:Omet'iklan CCG.jpg|thumb|Omet'iklan as he appears in the ''Star Trek Customizable Card Game'']] In the [[Pocket DS9]] novel ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine - Avatar|Avatar]]'', set in [[2376]], [[Ezri Dax]] thinks of Omet'iklan as an example of a mature and more disciplined Jem'Hadar when Elias Vaughn divulges information on some Starfleet research indicating Jem'Hadar became less violent and more disciplined as they age. Similarly in the novel ''[[Fearful Symmetry]]'', set in [[2377]], Benjamin Sisko cites Omet'iklan as an intelligent Jem'Hadar soldier who lacked free will just like [[Remata'Klan]] and [[Taran'atar]]. In an [[alternate timeline]] shown in the ''[[Echoes and Refractions]]'' novel ''A Gutted World'', Omet'iklan is one of the senior Jem'Hadar soldiers during an invasion of the [[Alpha Quadrant]] in [[2373]]. He is executed by the [[Founders]] after he destroys the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-E|-E}}, killing [[Odo]] in the process. Omet'iklan is also featured in the ''[[Star Trek Customizable Card Game]]'' which describes him as a "steely disciplinarian". ===External links=== * {{mbeta}} [[de:Omet'iklan]] [[es:Omet'iklan]] [[nl:Omet'iklan]] [[ru:Омет'иклан]] [[Category:Jem'Hadar]] [[Category:Dominion personnel]]

{{sidebar individual |image = Virak'kara.jpg |caption = Virak'kara (2372) |species = [[Jem'Hadar]] |affiliation = [[Dominion]] |occupation = [[Soldier]] in an unit under the command of [[Vorta]] [[Weyoun 4|Weyoun]] |status = Active |datestatus = 2372 |actor = [[Scott Haven]] }} {{aquote|How old are you?''"
"''I am eight.|[[Jadzia Dax]]''' and '''Virak'kara|2372|To the Death}} '''Virak'kara''' was a [[Jem'Hadar]] soldier in service of the [[Dominion]]. Created in [[2364]], Virak'kara was part of [[Omet'iklan]]'s unit in [[2372]] when their [[Jem'Hadar attack ship|attack ship]] was crippled by a rogue Jem'Hadar strike team. In the subsequent joint [[Starfleet]]-Jem'Hadar mission to destroy an [[Iconian gateway]] on [[Vandros IV]], Virak'kara was assigned to [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Jadzia Dax]]'s team. The two discussed the Jem'Hadar's reproductive process and their relatively short lifespan. Virak'kara, in turn, was taken aback by Dax's longevity as a [[Trill symbiont]]. He survived the mission and remained on Vandros IV to hunt down the remaining rogue Jem'Hadar. ({{DS9|To the Death}}) ==Memorable quote== "''If [[Jem'Hadar|we]] reach twenty, we are considered [[Honored Elder]]s... How old are you?''"
"''I stopped counting at 300.''"
"''...You don't look it.''"
"''Thank you.''" : - To [[Jadzia Dax]] on the {{USS|Defiant|2370}} {{bginfo|Virak'kara was played by [[Scott Haven]].}} [[cs:Virak'kara]] [[de:Virak'kara]] [[nl:Virak'kara]] [[Category:Dominion personnel]] [[Category:Jem'Hadar]]

{{sidebar individual |image = LamiraSon.jpg |caption = Limara'Son in early 2374 |species = [[Jem'Hadar]] |affiliation = [[Dominion]] |rank = [[Fourth]], later [[demotion|demoted]] to [[Sixth]] |occupation = Fourth, then Sixth, in command of an unit under [[Vorta]] [[Keevan]] |status = [[Deceased]] ([[KIA]]) |died = [[2374]],
[[Unnamed Alpha and Beta Quadrant planets#Dark matter nebula planet|Dark matter nebula planet]] |datestatus = 2374 |actor = [[Paul S. Eckstein]] }} '''Limara'Son''' was a [[Jem'Hadar]] soldier during the [[Dominion War]]. He served as the [[fourth]] under the [[Vorta]] [[Keevan]] in [[2374]]. That year, their [[ship]] [[crash land]]ed on a [[planet]] inside a [[dark matter nebula]]. Made anxious by lack of [[ketracel-white]], Limara'Son opened fire while reconnoitering a detachment of [[Starfleet]] [[officer]]s led by [[Captain]] [[Benjamin Sisko]], who had also crash-landed on the planet. {{dis|Third|rank}} [[Remata'Klan]] [[demotion|reduced]] him to [[sixth]] for disobeying his orders, though he refused to surrender the name of the disobedient soldier to Keevan when the Vorta demanded it, citing that, as the Jem'Hadar in charge of the detachment, he and he alone was responsible for disciplining the men. Limara'Son and the rest of the unit were killed in a deliberate ambush ordered by Keevan, and were buried on the planet. ({{DS9|Rocks and Shoals}}) {{bginfo|Limara'Son was played by [[Paul S. Eckstein]].|His name comes from the script.}} == External links == * {{Mbeta}} [[cs:Limara'Son]] [[de:Limara'Son]] [[fr:Limara'Son]] [[Category:Dominion personnel]] [[Category:Jem'Hadar]]

{{sidebar individual |image = YakTalon.jpg |caption = Yak'Talon |species = [[Jem'Hadar]] |rank = [[Jem'Hadar ranks#Seventh|Seventh]] |occupation = Seventh in command of an unit under [[Vorta]] [[Keevan]] |status = [[Deceased]] ([[KIA]]) |datestatus = 2374 |died = [[2374]],
[[Unnamed Alpha and Beta Quadrant planets#Dark matter nebula planet|Dark matter nebula planet]] |actor = [[Joe Murphy]] (uncredited)}} '''Yak'Talon''' was a [[Jem'Hadar]] [[soldier]] who served, in [[2374]], as the [[Seventh]] under the [[Vorta]] [[Keevan]] during the [[Dominion War]]. After [[Sisko's attack ship|their ship]] [[crash]]ed on a [[planet]] in a [[dark matter nebula]], located in [[Cardassian Union|Cardassian space]], he was assigned to repair their [[communications system]] so they could send a [[distress call]]. This task would have taken ten days, and the Jem'Hadar had insufficient [[ketracel-white]] to last until then. Yak'Talon and the rest of his unit were later killed in a deliberate ambush ordered by Keevan so that he himself could survive in [[Starfleet]] custody. ({{DS9|Rocks and Shoals}}) {{bginfo|Yak'Talon was played by [[Joe Murphy]].}} [[cs:Yak'Talon]] [[de:Yak'Talon]] [[es:Yak'Talon]] [[Category:Jem'Hadar]] [[Category:Dominion personnel]]

{{sidebar individual |image = Kudak'Etan.jpg |caption = Kudak'Etan |species = [[Jem'Hadar]] |affiliation = [[Dominion]] |rank = {{dis|First|rank}} |occupation = First in command of an unit under [[Vorta]] [[Gelnon]] |status = [[Deceased]], killed by [[Worf]] |died = [[2374]],
{{USS|Defiant|2370}} |datestatus = 2374 |actor = [[Scott Thompson Baker]] }} '''Kudak'Etan''' was a [[Jem'Hadar]] soldier bred for combat during the [[Dominion War]]. == History == In [[2374]], Kudak'Etan served as {{dis|First|rank}} under the [[Vorta]] [[supervisor]] [[Gelnon]]. One of the first Jem'Hadar to be bred in the [[Alpha Quadrant]], Kudak'Etan felt his "{{dis|Alpha|Jem'Hadar}}" genetic profile was superior to that of the "Gammas". It was this superiority that lead to him replacing former First [[Ixtana'Rax]] as the leader of his unit. Kudak'Etan's first mission as First was to assault the {{USS|Defiant|2370}} which was surveying a recently discovered [[subspace compression anomaly]]. He led a detachment of Jem'Hadar troops and was successful in capturing the Federation starship and piloting it back to [[Dominion]] territory. Against Ixtana'Rax's advice, Kudak'Etan allowed [[Captain]] [[Benjamin Sisko]] and a few of his officers access to the ship systems to repair the [[warp drive]] which had been damaged in the attack. They were able to delay the repairs long enough to regain system control, with some help from the [[runabout]] {{USS|Rubicon}} (which had been miniaturized by the anomaly). Kudak'Etan was later killed by [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Worf]] when they retook [[engineering]]. ({{DS9|One Little Ship}}) == Memorable quotes == "''It must be gratifying for an Elder to end his career with a victory. I feel privileged to be here with you at such a moment.''"
"''There is still much to do before we declare victory. Until we leave Federation space, we are vulnerable.''"
"''I am First. And I have declared victory.''"
:- '''Kudak'Etan''' and '''Ixtana'Rax''' "''Are you about to question my order, Second?''"
"''No. Obedience brings Victory.''"
"''And Victory is Life.''"
:- '''Kudak'Etan''' and '''Ixtana'Rax''' "''You are the Second. I am the First. Do not presume to tell me what to do.''"
:- '''Kudak'Etan''', to Ixtana'Rax "''We pledge our loyalties to the Founders from this-''"
"''Pah. We're all Alphas here. Our loyalty is demonstrated by our actions, not our words.''"
:- '''Lamat'ukan''' and '''Kudak'Etan''', during the white ceremony "''He should've listened to you and killed me when he had the chance.''"
"''He was a First. They don't need to listen. Obedience brings Victory and Victory is…''"
: '''Benjamin Sisko''' and '''Ixtana'Rax''', his final words before his death == Appendices == === Background information === [[File:Kudak'Etan costume - It's a Wrap.jpg|thumb|Baker's costume was later sold off for US$731.97 in the It's a Wrap sale and auction, complete with various prop extras]] Kudak'Etan was played by actor [[Scott Thompson Baker]]. The costume worn by Baker as Kudak'Etan was later sold off in the [[It's A Wrap! sale and auction]] for US$731.97, complete with various rubber accoutrements and a prop [[Kar'takin]] weapon. {{stala|5968}} The script for "One Little Ship" describes the pronunciation of the character's name as "koo-DAHK-eh-tahn". Additionally, it describes the Jem'Hadar as, "''an imposing figure, with vigor to his stride and an utter certainty that every step he takes is the right one. At his appearance Ixtana'Rax and the others snap to attention.''" {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/537.txt}} There were plans to further develop the animosity between Alpha and Gamma Jem'Hadar in later episodes of ''Deep Space Nine'' but the plotline was abandoned after "One Little Ship". No other mention of the two breeds is made. [[Ronald D. Moore]] regretted the decision, recalling, "''We dropped the ball on that one. It sounded like a cool idea at the time and we kept telling each other that we'd follow it up eventually, but it just kinda got away from us''". ("More from Moore", {{STM|54}}; {{AOLchat|Ronald D. Moore|ron129|1999}}) In his review of "One Little Ship", ''[[Star Trek]]'' author [[Keith R.A. DeCandido]] was critical of Kudak'Etan's character, writing, "''Kudak'etan does things, not because it's smart, but because he's enjoying snarking off Ixtana'rax – exactly the kind of petty stupidity that the Jem'Hadar have been mostly free of.''" {{el|tor.com/blogs/2014/09/star-trek-deep-space-nine-rewatch-qone-little-shipq}} === Apocrypha === Kudak'Etan is featured in the ''[[Star Trek Customizable Card Game]]'', which describes him as an "Arrogant First". === External links === * {{mbeta}} [[de:Kudak'Etan]] [[nl:Kudak'Etan]] [[Category:Dominion personnel]] [[Category:Jem'Hadar]]

{{sidebar individual |image = Ixtanarax.jpg |caption = Ixtana'Rax |species = [[Jem'Hadar]] |affiliation = [[Dominion]] |rank = [[Jem'Hadar ranks#Second|Second]] |occupation = Second in command of an unit under [[Vorta]] [[Gelnon]] |status = [[Deceased]], killed by [[Kira Nerys]] |datestatus = 2374 |born = c. [[2353]] |died = [[2374]],
{{USS|Defiant|2370}} |actor = [[Fritz Sperberg]] }} {{aquote|[[Kudak'Etan|The First]] may be a fool, but I am not.|Ixtana'Rax|2374|One Little Ship}} '''Ixtana'Rax''' was a [[Jem'Hadar]] [[soldier]] during the [[Dominion War]]. He had been the {{dis|First|rank}} under the [[Vorta]] [[Gelnon]], until he was replaced in [[2374]] by the "{{dis|Alpha|Jem'Hadar}}" [[Kudak'Etan]], becoming [[Jem'Hadar ranks#Second|Second]]. Ixtana'Rax was skeptical of the "Alphas" supposed superiority, stating that they had not yet proven themselves. He himself was an "[[Honored Elder]]", having survived more than [[2350s|twenty years]]. After his unit had captured the {{USS|Defiant|2370}}, Ixtana'Rax warned Kudak'Etan against allowing [[Captain]] [[Benjamin Sisko]] and his officers access to the ship, since it would give them an opportunity to retake the ship. Kudak'Etan overruled his recommendation, though Ixtana'Rax eventually discovered that the [[Starfleet]] officers had been hiding the extent of their repair work. Ixtana'Rax was again overruled when he advised that the system be checked for [[sabotage]] after the repairs were complete; as a result, the ship was nearly destroyed by a [[computer virus]] Sisko had programmed to activate when the [[warp drive]] was brought online. Fortunately, at that time the miniaturized [[runabout]] {{USS|Rubicon}} created a diversion and allowed the crew to retake [[engineering]]. Ixtana'Rax was shot by [[Major]] [[Kira Nerys]] in the fight. Sisko informed the dying Ixtana'Rax that Kudak'Etan should have listened to the Honored Elder from the start and killed Sisko when he had the chance. Ixtana'Rax died speaking the Jem'Hadar [[creed]]. ({{DS9|One Little Ship}}) {{bginfo|Ixtana'Rax was played by actor [[Fritz Sperberg]].|His name comes from the script.}} ==External link== *{{mbeta}} [[de:Ixtana'Rax]] [[es:Ixtana'Rax]] [[Category:Dominion personnel]] [[Category:Jem'Hadar]]

'''Lamat'Ukan''' was a [[Jem'Hadar]] soldier during the [[Dominion War]] and also an "{{dis|Alpha|Jem'Hadar}}", one of the first Jem'Hadar to be bred in the [[Alpha Quadrant]]. 

In [[2374]], he served as [[Kudak'Etan]]'s {{dis|Third|rank}}, under the [[Vorta]] [[Gelnon]]. Lamat'Ukan participated in the assault which captured the {{USS|Defiant|2370}}. Kudak'Etan planned to have Lamat'Ukan replace [[Ixtana'Rax]] as his {{dis|Second|rank}} after their current mission, since he was pleased with Lamat'Ukan's initiative. Lamat'Ukan was subdued when the ''Defiant'' crew regained control and flooded the ship with [[anesthezine]] [[gas]]. He was later sent to a [[Federation]] [[prisoner of war]] camp. ({{DS9|One Little Ship}})

==Appendices==
=== Background information ===
Lamat'Ukan was portrayed by [[Christian Zimmerman]]. The character's name comes from the script for the episode. {{st-minutiae|resources/scripts/537.txt}}

=== Apocrypha ===
In the backstory of ''[[Star Trek Online]]'', [[Odo]] ordered the Jem'Hadar remaining in the Alpha Quadrant to return to the Gamma Quadrant, but Lamat'Ukan and his subordinates refused, regarding Odo as a false god. They were later hired by [[Gul]] [[Madred]] as security for his mining operations in the [[Septimus III|Septimus system]]. In the game proper, he is killed when the player character attacks his stronghold on [[Orias III]] in the mission "The New Link".

{{sidebar individual |image = Goran'Agar.jpg |caption = Goran'Agar (2372) |species = [[Jem'Hadar]] |affiliation = [[Dominion]] |rank = {{dis|First|rank}} |occupation = [[Soldier]] |status = Active |datestatus = 2372 |actor = [[Scott MacDonald]] }} '''Goran'Agar''' was a [[Jem'Hadar]] {{dis|First|rank}}, whose [[ship]] [[crash land]]ed on the [[planet]] [[Bopak III]] in [[2369]]. He was the only survivor, but had only enough [[ketracel-white]] to last three days. Goran'Agar stretched the supply to eight, but did not die afterwards as he expected. He was rescued thirty-five days later, and he assumed that something on the planet had cured him of his [[addiction]]. Hoping to free the rest of his men from control by the [[Vorta]], Goran'Agar left the [[Dominion]] and led them back to Bopak III in [[2372]]. Unfortunately, they remained addicted to the white, and Goran'Agar was unable to determine the cause. An unexpected opportunity came to him in the form of [[Doctor]] [[Julian Bashir]] and [[Chief]] [[Miles O'Brien]], who had landed on the planet to investigate a [[subspace]] [[magneton pulse]] being generated by the Jem'Hadar ship's engines. Goran'Agar ordered their capture and told Bashir of their situation, compelling him to work to find a solution. Eventually, Bashir postulated that Goran'Agar had not been cured by the planet, but rather possessed some type of genetic [[mutation]] which allowed his body to produce the white it required; while he had always taken white with other Jem'Hadar, he had never actually ''needed'' it. After O'Brien escaped custody and destroyed Bashir's equipment, Goran'Agar realized that there was no choice but death for his men. He decided to release the [[Starfleet]] [[officer]]s and hunt down the remaining Jem'Hadar himself, to give them a quick finish in combat rather than a slow death from lack of white. '''Kazago''' was the [[first officer]] aboard a [[Ferengi]] {{Class|D'Kora}} [[Bok's Marauder|marauder]] [[CO|commanded]] by [[DaiMon]] [[Bok]] in [[2364]]. 

He was involved in the plan to return the {{USS|Stargazer|NCC-2893}} to Starfleet, unaware that Bok was not planning to sell it but to use it to avenge the death of [[Bok's son 001|Bok's son]] who was killed in a [[Battle of Maxia|battle with the ''Stargazer'']] in [[2355]], by gaining revenge on [[Federation]] [[captain]] [[Jean-Luc Picard]] of the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-D|-D}}.

After connecting, first officer to first officer, with [[Commander]] [[William T. Riker]], Riker was able to convince Kazago that Bok was pursing an unprofitable venture. Once Riker proved this to be the case, by presenting one of Bok's [[thought maker]]s, Kazago relieved Bok from command and placed him under guard. ({{TNG|The Battle}})

'''Mordoc''' was a [[Ferengi]] who served under [[DaiMon]] [[Tarr]] aboard [[Tarr's Marauder|his Marauder]] in [[2364]].

Along with the rest of the crew, Mordoc participated in the [[theft]] of a [[T-9 energy converter]] from [[Gamma Tauri IV]]. Mordoc, along with [[Letek]] and [[Kayron]], later [[beam]]ed down to a [[planet]] in the [[Delphi Ardu system]], after their [[starship]] was immobilized above the [[planet]] by a powerful [[force field]]. He and the other members of the Ferengi [[science team]] ambushed [[William T. Riker|Riker]] and his [[away team]] during [[first contact]] with them on the planet. 

During the encounter, he was disgusted by [[Natasha Yar]], as not only was a [[woman]] allowed to serve on a [[starship]], but she also wore [[clothing|clothes]]. Later commenting to [[Portal 63]] how, in the example of Yar, were "''inviting others to unclothe them,''" calling it "''the very depth of [[perversion]].''" He then told Yar, who had just told him to keep his [[paw]]s off, that "''no female, Human or Ferengi, can order Mordoc around!''" before ordering her to "''Submit!''" 

Finally, after an understanding was reached between Portal and Riker in favor of the Humans over the Ferengi, specifically after a discussion referencing a quote from [[Sun Tzu]], Mordoc claimed that "''The truth is, I gave those words to this Human.''" ({{TNG|The Last Outpost}})

Mordoc was part of [[Commander]] [[William T. Riker]]'s memories while being infected on the surface of [[Surata IV]] and treated in [[sickbay]]. ({{TNG|Shades of Gray}})

{{bginfo|Mordoc was played by actor [[Jake Dengel]].}}

'''Grish''' was a [[Ferengi]] [[pirate]] who worked with [[Ulis]] in [[2151]].

Grish and two other Ferengi helped Ulis in an attempt to pillage {{EnterpriseNX}}, once they had rendered its crew unconscious with [[anesthesia gas]].

After being awakened by [[Commander]] [[Charles Tucker III|Tucker]], who was unaffected by the [[Anesthesia|anesthetic]] used by the Ferengi, [[Sub-Commander]] [[T'Pol]] was able to convince [[Muk]] that Ulis was trying to rob him of his share of the profits. Grish's greed motivated him to trust Tucker, who led him, Ulis, and Muk into a trap, where they were ambushed by T'Pol.

Upon recovering, Grish and the other Ferengi were forced to carry all the items they had loaded onto their own ship back onto the ''Enterprise''. They were then allowed to leave aboard their vessel, with [[Krem]], a Ferengi who had been treated with disrespect by the others, now in command. ({{ENT|Acquisition}})

{{bginfo|Grish was played by [[Matt Malloy]].|In the final draft script of "Acquisition", Grish was initially described as "a meeker Ferengi [than Muk] who does what he's told."}}

'''Parth''' was a [[Ferengi]] who worked as the [[hug-cierge]] of the [[Lobe's Lodge]] [[hotel]] on [[Ferenginar]] in the late [[24th century]]. One aspect of his job was to enforce [[Ferengi law]] regarding [[fraud]], for which he was empowered to condemn violators to a lifetime of hard labor in the [[subaquatic sulfur mine]]s.

In [[2381]], when [[Lieutenants jg]] [[D'Vana Tendi]] and [[Sam Rutherford]] were assigned to pretend to be a [[married]] couple for [[travel guide]] duty on [[Ferenginar]], Parth managed their all-inclusive [[newlywed]] [[discount]] package at Lobe's Lodge. As their "hug-cierge", he aggressively oversaw their prescribed romantic activities, including a [[photo session]] and a [[meal]] at [[Quark's Federation Experience Bar & Grill]].

As Parth led Tendi and Rutherford to a [[blind box]] for them to [[sex (intercourse)|consummate]] their marriage, [[Migleemo]] inadvertently exposed their ruse by calling them [[platonic]] [[friend]]s. The two managed to bluff their way free by claiming that they had both been involved with Migleemo, and were thus opting to [[divorce]]. Parth then offered Migleemo their [[homewrecker]] package. ({{LD|Parth Ferengi's Heart Place}})
